text: dsh-tunnelmux-remote 是面向 DSH Web 的手机远程访问插件。它在侧边栏提供扫码配对入口，并提供 /m 移动界面和 TunnelMux 隧道状态面板。用户可在手机查看、搜索和创建会话，阅读对话、发送消息、重命名会话及切换模型；配对设备可从面板管理。适合需要从手机继续使用 DSH Web 的用户。需要 DSH Web profile 和本机 TunnelMux daemon；自动隧道默认关闭。

dsh-tunnelmux-remote enables phone access to DSH web. Pair from a sidebar QR code, then use /m to browse and search sessions, read conversations, send messages, rename sessions, and select models. A panel shows pairing and TunnelMux status. Requires a DSH web profile and local TunnelMux daemon.
想用手机扫码连接到正在运行的 DSH Web。
我想在手机上查看和搜索 DSH 会话，并接着发消息。
How can I pair my phone and continue a DSH web conversation remotely?
dsh-tunnelmux-remote 的功能「手机会话」：配对后可在 /m 查看和搜索会话、打开对话、发送消息、重命名会话并切换模型；界面通过宿主 API 代理读取和更新会话。
dsh-tunnelmux-remote 的功能「扫码远程配对」：从 DSH 侧边栏打开远程控制面板，查看配对二维码和设备状态；插件可调用本地 TunnelMux 控制 API 启动隧道并显示状态。
dsh-tunnelmux-remote 使用前须知：自动隧道会通过 TunnelMux 将本地 DSH Web 地址接入 cloudflared 或 ngrok 公共入口；控制 API 支持可选 Bearer token。

dsh-tunnelmux-remote README · dsh-tunnelmux-remote：Mobile remote control for the DeepSeek Harness web GUI, with **TunnelMux as the
tunnel backend**. Scan a QR code beside the sidebar to pair your phone, chat
with your sessions from /m, and revoke any device at any time. The public URL
comes from the local TunnelMux control API (cloudflared/ngrok) — no embedded
tunnel binary in the plugin.

dsh-tunnelmux-remote README · dsh-tunnelmux-remote：Built from scratch (2026-08-16) following the design in
[TunnelMux docs/plans/2026-08-16-dsh-tunnelmux-remote-design.md](https://github.com/kexuejin/TunnelMux/blob/main/docs/plans/2026-08-16-dsh-tunnelmux-remote-design.md)
and referencing @linxin666/dsh-remote-web-ui (Apache-2.0) for the pairing model.

dsh-tunnelmux-remote README · Features：- **Scan-to-pair QR** beside the official sidebar footer: one-time token, first
  accept consumes it, refresh invalidates the old QR immediately.
- **Device sessions**: HttpOnly cookie gate, presence tracking with offline
  detection, max 4 devices (oldest evicted), revoke all with one click.
- **Mobile surface** at `/m`: a real phone client — session list with cursor
  pagination and content search, conversation view rebuilt from the session log
  (user / assistant / tool activity, streaming tail, compaction replacements),
  send, rename, and model switching — bridged through the host apiProxy with a
  strict method allowlist. See [Phone surface](#phone-surface).
- **TunnelMux backend**: `POST /v1/tunnel/start` returns the public URL
  synchronously (daemon waits for provider startup); the plugin **observes**
  status for the panel and never restarts the tunnel itself — the daemon owns
  `auto_restart`.
- **Live updates**: SSE `/api/pair/events` for the desktop panel and
  `/m/api/events.mux` for the phone.
- **Desktop browser pairing**: opens the real GUI on the public URL, not just
  the phone page — see [Desktop bridge](#desktop-bridge-bro

dsh-tunnelmux-remote README · Install：Requires a running TunnelMux daemon (control API on 127.0.0.1:4765) and the DSH
web profile:

```bash
cd ~/.dsh/profiles/web
dsh plugin add github:kexuejin/dsh-tunnelmux-remote   # or link:/path/to/this/repo
```

Or add to `cordis.patch.yml` manually:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: tunnelmux-remote
      name: dsh-tunnelmux-remote
```

dsh-tunnelmux-remote README · Configuration (settings namespace `tunnelmux-remote`)：| key | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | master switch |
| `tunnelmuxBaseUrl` | `http://127.0.0.1:4765` | TunnelMux control API |
| `tunnelmuxApiToken` | `''` (secret) | optional Bearer token |
| `targetUrl` | `http://127.0.0.1:3080` | local GUI the tunnel exposes |
| `tunnelProvider` | `cloudflared` | `cloudflared` or `ngrok` |
| `autoTunnel` | `false` | start the tunnel on plugin load |
| `publicBaseUrl` | `''` | existing public entry (skips auto-tunnel) |
| `tokenTtlMs` / `offlineAfterMs` / `maxDevices` | 10min / 25s / 4 | pairing tuning |
| `cookieName` | `dsh_pair` | device cookie |
| `mobileEnterToSend` | `true` | Enter sends in the phone chat box |
| `desktopBridge` | `true` | start the loopback pairing bridge |
| `bridgePort` | `3988` | bridge listen port (127.0.0.1 only) |
| `bridgeRedirect` | `/` | where the browser goes after pairing |
| `bridgeDays` | `30` | minted cookie lifetime in days (≤ DSH `cookieMaxAgeDays`) |
| `registerRoutes` | `true` | upsert the two TunnelMux routes on load |
| `pairRouteId` / `pairRoutePrefix` | `deepseek` / `/deepseek` | gated entry

dsh-tunnelmux-remote README · Phone surface：`/m` is three static routes and one RPC channel, all behind the paired-device
cookie: the shell (`/m`), its stylesheet (`/m/mobile.css`), and the bundle
(`/m/mobile.js`, react inlined so the phone needs no module loader).

dsh-tunnelmux-remote README · Phone surface：**The conversation is rebuilt from the session log**, the same way the desktop
client does it, in `src/mobile-app/transcript.ts`: `session.history` seeds the
surface, the mirrored mux appends to it, and `surfaceOp` replacements (a
compaction summary) collapse the nodes they shadow. Streaming text is shown from
`assistant/chunk` deltas and retired when the assembled `assistant/message`
lands; a tool call shows as running until its result pairs by `callId`. Replayed
events are dropped by `seq`, and a sequence gap reloads the window instead of
rendering a hole. A sent message is echoed optimistically and reconciled against
the durable `user/message` event through the `rpcId` the host passes back.

dsh-tunnelmux-remote README · Phone surface：**Display adaptation** is the point of the surface, so the decisions are
recorded rather than left in the stylesheet:

dsh-tunnelmux-remote README · Phone surface：- **Notches and home indicators** — the shell declares `viewport-fit=cover`, and
  the header and composer consume `env(safe-area-inset-*)`.
- **The on-screen keyboard** — the app frame is sized in `dvh` and the shell asks
  for `interactive-widget=resizes-content`, so the composer stays on screen
  instead of being covered while the transcript scrolls independently.
- **Both colour schemes** — every colour is a custom property, redefined under
  `prefers-color-scheme: dark`, with the browser chrome following through two
  `theme-color` metas. No colour literal exists outside `styles.ts`.
- **Touch** — controls are at least 44px, hover styling is gated behind
  `(hover: hover)`, pressed feedback is a `:active` change, and
  `prefers-reduced-motion` drops the animations.
- **Zoom stays available.** An earlier `user-scalable=no` is gone.
- **Width** — nothing sets a fixed pixel width, one column and 16px insets carry
  a 360px phone, and from 900px the list and the conversation sit side by side.

dsh-tunnelmux-remote README · Phone surface：Known limits of this surface: the host event stream is not proxied, so a session
created on the desktop appears after the list's 刷新 button rather than on its
own; `session.cancel` and the queue mutations are outside the allowlist, so a
running turn cannot be stopped from the phone; images are announced but not
shown; and the 回车发送/回车换行 toggle applies to the current visit, because
`mobile.preferences` is read-only over `/m/api`.

dsh-tunnelmux-remote README · Desktop bridge (browser sessions over the public URL)：The QR flow pairs a phone with `/m`. Opening the **full GUI** in a real browser
over the public URL needs something else: a DSH browser-session cookie. The
bridge mints one, so a visitor who passes the access gate lands in the app
already signed in. It replaces the standalone `~/.dsh/bin/dsh-web-cookie` tool
— you no longer run a second process by hand.

dsh-tunnelmux-remote README · Desktop bridge (browser sessions over the public URL)：```
browser ──► https://host/deepseek          (TunnelMux asks for the access code)
              └─► 127.0.0.1:3988           (bridge: sets cookies, JS redirect)
                    └─► https://host/      (the GUI, already authenticated)
```

dsh-tunnelmux-remote README · Desktop bridge (browser sessions over the public URL)：- **Cookies are minted offline.** The HMAC secret under
  `client-connection/browser-session` in `$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml` is
  persistent, unlike the per-launch `?token=`, so a minted cookie survives
  restarts of both the app and the tunnel.
- **Two routes, both upserted idempotently.** `/deepseek` points at the bridge
  (strip prefix), `/` points at the GUI (no strip). The root entry is not
  decoration: the DSH client builds root-absolute URLs from `location.origin`,
  so under a path mount every RPC asked the tunnel host for `/api/...` and came
  back empty — session list included. Routing around it is the point, because
  the client is not modifiable.
- **The gate code is carried across.** On pairing the bridge also installs
  `tunnelmux_access_<routeId>` for both routes (from the daemon's state file),
  so passing the gate once unlocks `/deepseek` and `/` together.
- **A locked control plane is not fatal.** If the daemon answers 401, route
  sync is deferred and logged; routes persist in the daemon state file and
  apply once it is unlocked.

dsh-tunnelmux-remote README · Security model：- **One active token**; `issue()` replaces it, so a fresh QR invalidates the
  previous link immediately.
- **One-time accept**; reuse returns `used` (409). Tokens expire (default
  10 min). `stop()` revokes every session and clears the token — the phone's
  next gated request gets 403.
- **Fences**: control endpoints (`issue`/`stop`/`events`) are loopback-only;
  phone endpoints (`accept`/`heartbeat`/`status`) allow loopback, LAN
  literals, or the public tunnel Host. Accept is rate-limited per IP
  (10 attempts / 30 s).
- **Mobile allowlist**: only `workspace.list`, `session.*` and
  `mobile.preferences` are exposed over `/m/api`; everything else 403s.
  `settings.*` / `credentials.*` remain loopback-only host methods and are
  never reachable from a phone.
- **The bridge is a bearer-token dispenser.** Anyone who can reach it gets a
  valid DSH session, so it binds `127.0.0.1` only and **must** sit behind an
  access-gated route (`registerRoutes` puts the access code in front of
  `/deepseek` for exactly this reason). Exposing port 3988 directly — by
  disabling the gate, or by adding an ungated route to it — hands out full

npm install
npm run typecheck   # tsc client (+ jsdom tests) + host
npm test            # vitest (99 tests)
npm run build       # tsdown: lib/index.js (host) + lib/mobile.js + client/client.js

dsh-tunnelmux-remote README · Development：The phone surface is gated without a browser: `test/mobile-display.test.ts`
pins the head and the stylesheet's display contract, `test/mobile-styles.test.ts`
fails when the markup uses a class the stylesheet does not define or writes a
colour literal outside `styles.ts`, `test/transcript.test.ts` covers the surface
fold, and `test/dom/mobile-app.test.tsx` mounts the page in jsdom and asserts the
prompt payload the host actually receives.
